q7.answer: On the live path, progress is the Kafka offsets of group indexer-live, committed only after every document in a batch is resolved (applied, counted stale, or produced to the DLQ with the ack received). On the rebuild, the job state, S, the replay start and last_id are in the indexer's own Postgres, and last_id is saved after each 1000-row batch is indexed; the replay group indexer-rebuild commits its Kafka offsets after each of its batches.

q8.answer: Nothing in the crashed batch's offsets was committed, so after restart the same batch is read again and the documents are retried. Re-sent writes are safe because the version is commit_lsn: documents already applied at that version are accepted again, and any older write is refused as a stale 409 and counted.

q9.answer: Changes committed after the snapshot point S have commit_lsn greater than S, and the rebuild group indexer-rebuild replays the topic from the stored replay start (snapshot start minus 10 minutes, per partition), applying each event to products_v4 with version = commit_lsn. Changes before S are already in the snapshot, and older replayed events are refused as stale, so nothing is lost. The plan does not say how a timestamp becomes a per-partition Kafka offset, so that step still needs to be defined.

q10.answer: Every document written by the bulk copy carries version = S, the value of pg_current_wal_lsn() read at the start of the repeatable-read snapshot, converted to the same 64-bit integer as commit_lsn. Replayed events with a commit_lsn at or after S then supersede it, and older ones are refused as stale.

q11.answer: After cutover the live consumer dual-writes to products_v4 and products_v3 and commits offsets only when both acknowledge, so v3 stays current with no gap and a single atomic alias request can move products and products_write back to it. The protection ends when 48 hours pass with no rollback: writes to products_v3 stop and the index is deleted. A rollback restarts a new 48-hour window with v4 as the standby.

q12.answer: Search is unaffected in both cases, because the alias products still points to products_v3 and the live path keeps writing v3 until the alias move; products_v4 has no alias and the search API never queries it. A crash during the copy resumes from saved last_id under a new snapshot S2 with the replay start unchanged, and a failing catch-up keeps replaying until the gate passes, times out into a reconcile sweep, or the rebuild is abandoned and v4 deleted. The plan does not say what happens if the cutover fails between pausing the live group and moving the alias, so the live group could stay paused and that needs a recovery step.
